title: Financial Statement Audits and Data Breaches
eligible_reason: Two staggered binary treatments at the auditor level, each estimated in a first column with client-auditor-pair and year fixed effects and no controls (reghdfe breach_info TREAT, a(year firm_aud) cl(auditor_fkey)): Table 4 col 1 uses it_insp (= 1 from the year the client's auditor is first cited in PCAOB inspection reports for IT-related deficiencies; auditor-level inspection years 2003-2015, 8 distinct switch-on years inside the 2004-2016 panel, 906 never-treated pairs) and Table 5 col 1 uses interaction (= treat x 1(year >= learning_min_year), auditors' learning from other clients' breaches; 11 cohorts 2006-2016, 6,079 never-treated pairs). Remaining columns, Table 6 and the Figure 2 event studies add time-varying controls (ln_ta loss intangible) and are excluded.
design_notes: Client-firm x auditor pair (firm_aud) by fiscal year panel, 2004-2016, restricted to integrated-audit clients (merge inte_audit.dta on gvkey year; keep if inte==1; inte is a time-varying accelerated-filer status used only as a sample restriction). Outcome breach_info is a 0/1 data-breach indicator (mean 1.5%), estimated by linear regression. Table 4 (pcaob_it_analysis.dta): it_insp monotone within firm_aud; it_insp == 1(year>=it_insp_year) for 98.9% of rows; 7,606 pairs: 6,291 always treated (Big-4 and other auditors inspected 2003-2004), 906 never treated, 409 switchers; auditor-level it_insp_year: 2003 (4 auditors), 2004 (4), 2005 (3), 2007 (2), 2008 (2), 2011 (2), 2012 (1), 2013 (3), 2014 (4), 2015 (1); 280 of 306 auditors never cited. Table 5 (auditor_learning_data.dta): interaction = treat x post(learning_min_year), treat = 23% of rows, learning_min_year auditor specific 2005-2015; 757 always treated, 6,079 never treated, 770 switchers; monotone for 98.9% of pairs. Table 6: subsample splits (firm_erp, good_committee, firm_ic_weak) with controls. Figure 2: event-study with leads/lags up to 18 on a fillin-balanced panel, with controls. Tables 2-3 are descriptive regressions with controls (Table 3: auditor switches big_pos_1N##big_treat with cik and year FE and controls).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Table 4 (it_insp): switch-on years inside the panel at the auditor level: 2005, 2007, 2008, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015 (8 cohorts) plus always-treated auditors inspected in 2003-2004. Table 5 (interaction): firm_aud-level first-treated years 2006-2016 (11 cohorts; 719 pairs in 2006) plus 757 always-treated pairs.

specs.outcome: breach_info (1 if the firm has a data breach in year t)
specs.treatment_definition: 1 from the year the client's auditor is first mentioned in PCAOB inspection reports for IT-related audit deficiencies (auditor-level it_insp_year), 0 before; absorbing
specs.sample_condition: pcaob_it_analysis.dta merged m:1 gvkey year with inte_audit.dta (drop _m==2, inte=0 if missing), keep if inte==1; 43,996 pair-years
specs.notes: Column 2 adds ln_ta loss intangible. Large always-treated share (83% of pairs). Few treated clusters: leverage screen likely binding.

specs.treatment_var: interaction (= treat x 1(year >= learning_min_year); components treat, learning_min_year)
specs.treatment_definition: 1 for clients whose auditor has other clients in other geographic areas that experienced a data breach, from the auditor's first such learning year (learning_min_year, 2005-2015) onward; 0 otherwise
specs.sample_condition: auditor_learning_data.dta merged with inte_audit.dta, keep if inte==1; 43,996 pair-years
specs.notes: interaction reverts to 0 for ~1% of pairs after first treatment; drop those rows per protocol. Columns 2-3 add controls (col 3 uses interaction2, other clients regardless of geography).

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls ln_ta loss intangible in every column; Table 6 also splits by firm characteristics
specs.reported_location: Table 4 col 2; Table 5 cols 2-3; Table 6 Panels A-B

specs.exclusion_reason: event-study with time-varying controls (loss intangible ln_ta); estimated on a fillin-balanced panel with 18 leads/lags, lead1 set to 0
specs.treatment_var: ind_treat_lead* ind_treat ind_treat_lag* (Panel A); interaction_lead* interaction interaction_lag* (Panel B)
specs.notes: Near-miss: dropping the controls would give an eligible unstacked event study.

data_files_note: README: 'The Data folder contains all the data required for the final analysis'. Compustat/Audit Analytics-derived, shipped in full.
priority_note: Eligible, data shipped. Rare binary outcome and few treated clusters (26 of 306 auditors in Table 4) may trigger the leverage screen.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Cohorts and monotonicity verified in the shipped .dta files after reproducing the merge and inte==1 restriction in Python. Column numbers follow the do-file order (col 1 without controls); verify against the article.
